title.narrative: Strengthened tripartite capacity to improve labour migration governance and address child labour in Eswatini

description.narrative: Following the launch of the National Labour Migration Policy in 2025, Eswatini is strengthening labour migration governance in response to fragmented institutional coordination that increases vulnerability for migrant workers. A tripartite national steering committee has been established to provide strategic oversight of policy implementation but requires enhanced capacity to effectively fulfil its mandate. Challenges are further compounded by misalignment between national legislation and international labour migration standards, with implications for the protection of migrant workers’ rights. In partnership with the International Organization for Migration, ILO support is being provided to strengthen the oversight capacity of the national migration steering committee and to advance legislative and policy alignment with Conventions 97 and 143, including consideration of ratification. The primary beneficiaries of this intervention are migrant workers, employers, workers and the Government. In addition, ILO supervisory bodies have identified persistent gaps in Eswatini’s legal and enforcement framework on child labour, despite existing policy commitments. Working with the Intersectoral Committee on Child Labour and tripartite partners, ILO support is directed towards finalising the review of the National Action Programme on Child Labour to address the concerns of the ILO’s Standards Supervisory bodies, and to ensure alignment with the Durban Call to Action. The primary targeted groups for this intervention are children, workers, employers and government.
